kevin: pushed an nsys snapshot from prod-node-7 after the 11:04 UTC spike. summary: matmul launches get serialized because workspace probing triggers cudaMalloc/free on the default stream when no reserved workspace is configured.

maria: can you share the exact repro command and runtime flags? are we running the slab allocator or the legacy allocator in that cluster?

kevin: repro I ran locally:```
./run_probe --model=gpt-medium --seq=1536 --batch=1 --iters=250 --warmup=40 --profile=nsys --cublaslt_workspace_limit=0 --allocator=legacy
```
Cluster had dynamic config that sets cublaslt_workspace_limit=0 to reduce reserved memory for multi-tenant experiments.

ivan: that matches our expectations: when cublasLt can't use a reserved workspace it falls back to cudaMalloc for some algos during probing/launch. our current legacy allocator issues those mallocs on the default stream which forces inter-stream synchronization.

kevin: pasted a condensed nsys timeline snippet:```
[stream 0] cudaMemcpyHtoD 0.5ms -> cublasLtMatmul id=3 10.8ms -> cudaFree 1.2ms -> cudaMalloc 2.9ms -> cublasLtMatmul id=7 11.9ms
[stream 5] cublasLtMatmul id=0 9.4ms -> cudaMemcpyDtoH 0.4ms
(note many small malloc/free spikes interleaved with matmuls).
```

maria: did you correlate with KV cache behavior? maybe session start is allocating ephemeral KV buffers which compound fragmentation.

kevin: yes, around the same timestamps we see KV cache miss handlers allocate 4-12MB ephemeral tensors then free them shortly after. with workspace mallocs we get fragmentation + longer allocation latencies.

perf-bot: regression summary: baseline tag 2140009876 median matmul=2.05ms, current run median=3.28ms (+60%). allocation/syscalls contribute ~30-40% of the extra time.

ivan: possible mitigations: 1) reserve a small persistent workspace (mempool) per-device so cublasLt can use preallocated buffers; 2) switch allocator to cudaMallocAsync or a per-stream free list to avoid default-stream sync; 3) prefer zero-workspace algos for tiny-batch low-latency cases via policy.

jen: ops workaround: stage a config that sets cublaslt_workspace_limit=16MB and enable slab allocator on dedicated clusters for next week rollout. that should reduce malloc/free churn quickly.

kevin: quick local results: legacy allocator + workspace_limit=0: matmul median=3.3ms, p99 ~41ms. slab allocator + 16MB reserved workspace: median=1.9ms, p99 ~17ms. sample algo table from profiler:```
algos:
  0: implicit_gemm, ws=0, t=1.8ms
  4: tiled_kernel, ws=6MB, t=1.5ms
  9: splitk_variant, ws=10MB, t=1.4ms (needs alloc if no pool)
policy suggestion: if reserved_ws>=6MB pick id4 else pick id0 for batch=1
```

maria: careful: implicit_gemm isn't always faster for longer sequences. we should make the policy conditional on seq_len and batch size (e.g., implicit for batch<=1 && seq<=1024).

ivan: agreed. also note that switching to cudaMallocAsync (CUDA 11.4+) removes serialization in our tests because allocations are deferred and freed per-stream; however some older nodes/AMIs in our fleet might not support it. we should gate that behind a capability check.

jen: ops, are older AMIs compatible with cudaMallocAsync?

ops-bot: created INF-3123 assigned->eng-runtime: "Investigate matmul allocation stalls: try mempool + cudaMallocAsync + KV warmup".

perf-bot: attached traces: baseline_nsight_2140009876.zip vs spike_nsight_2167894321.zip. hotspots at 00:11:03 and 00:11:07.

ivan: next action items:
- kevin: add telemetry counters workspace_malloc_count and kv_ephemeral_alloc_count + histogram for allocation latencies
- jen: rollout config: enable slab allocator + reserve 16MB workspace on dedicated clusters (staged)
- maria: implement runtime rollout policy: prefer zero-ws algos for batch<=1 && seq_len<=1024; otherwise use workspace algos when mempool present
- ivan: prototype allocator branch with cudaMallocAsync fallback and per-stream free lists
- kevin: add a small KV-cache warmup on session start to preallocate a tiny prefix to avoid first-request spikes

kevin: small patch I tested:```diff
- if (!reserved_ws) cudaMalloc(&buf, needed);
+ if (!reserved_ws) buf = mempool->alloc_stream(stream, needed);
```
worked in local runs. i'll push a PR and attach the nsys flame link to INF-3123.

maria: also add an e2e perf test in our CI matrix that exercises batch=1, seq in [256,1024,1536] with allocator variations so we catch regressions.

jen: i'll schedule the staged rollout and k8s window. thanks all, please keep INF-3123 updated with rollouts and telem.

kevin: will follow up with post-rollout traces. expecting p99 improvements once mempool+slab is enabled.
